clue.text: Bend almost all of shield

indicators.note: almost all of something means it is taken short of its final letter

blocks.note: a buckler is a small round shield

explanation.surface: A battered shield, nearly all of it bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCKLER loses its last letter to leave BUCKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle is to bend or crumple under pressure, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: British philosopher clipped son in European capital

indicators.note: something clipped is trimmed, so the name loses its final letter

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
Bertrand Russell, British philosopher
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A British thinker with a short-haired son living abroad in a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Brussels is the capital of Belgium and seat of the European Union institutions.

clue.text: Type of sideboard in study — there's a silly craze involving it

indicators.note: silly means foolish or disordered, so the word after it is rearranged
involving means taking in, so the jumble wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A sideboard in someone's study has become a passing fashion craze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the study, which is what the jumbled word surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A credenza is an Italian-style sideboard or low cabinet, a kind of serving furniture.

clue.text: European city, for example, featured in story

indicators.note: something featured in a work appears inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A city in Europe, used as an example in some tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a large city in eastern Belgium, on the river Meuse.

clue.text: Demanding higher prices at college fair

blocks.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
a fair or market is a gathering for selling goods

explanation.surface: Stallholders at a college fair are charging steep prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' for being at university is a British usage, as in going up to Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket goods aim at wealthier buyers, so they carry higher price tags.

clue.text: Salute existing members

blocks.note: present means existing now
arms are limbs, also called members

explanation.surface: Greeting the people who currently belong to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Members reads as club members but means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Present arms is the military salute in which a rifle is held upright before the body.

clue.text: Flower in book

definitions.note: describes where it appears rather than naming it

blocks.note: first meaning: a tall plant such as great mullein
second meaning: the staff that blossomed in the Bible's Book of Numbers

explanation.walkthrough: The 'book' is the Bible, where the rod of Moses's brother sprouted blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to several tall spiky flowering plants, and also to the miraculous staff of Moses's brother in scripture.

clue.text: Article is penned by King, Queen and Emperor!

indicators.note: something penned by others is shut in like an animal in a pen, so it goes inside

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a is the indefinite article
taken as written
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A piece of writing composed by a king, a queen and an emperor together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double work in the surface but is one of the inserted pieces, alongside the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaiser is the German title for an emperor, from Latin Caesar.

clue.text: International edition is critically examined

blocks.note: a Test is an international match in cricket or rugby
ed. is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: An overseas edition of a book gets a harsh review.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tested has been put through trials and scrutinised closely.

clue.text: A Parisian, still inconsistent

blocks.note: UN is French for 'a'
even as an intensifier, as in 'even/still better'

explanation.surface: A Parisian who remains unreliable in behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uneven varies in quality, so it is inconsistent or irregular.

clue.text: Narrowly avoided collision with tight young woman

blocks.note: near can mean stingy, tight with money
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A near crash involving a young woman who had been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' reads as drunk in the surface, but it means mean with money, which is the old sense of near.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an incident where a collision almost happened but was avoided.

clue.text: Adam's mate and daughter locked in warehouse with dock worker

indicators.note: things locked in a place are shut inside it, so the earlier pieces go inside

blocks.note: a store is a warehouse
Eve was Adam's partner in Genesis
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Eve and her daughter shut in a warehouse along with a docker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships, a dock worker by another name.

clue.text: Dickens character, Violet, abused, nursing broken wrist

indicators.note: something abused is mistreated and knocked out of shape, so the name is rearranged
a broken thing is in pieces that can be put back in another order
nursing means holding close, so the first jumble cradles the second

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mistreated woman named Violet tends someone's fractured wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the orphan hero of Charles Dickens's novel of the same name.

clue.text: Relative, European, located in Riviera resort

indicators.note: something located in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A family member from Europe living in a smart Riviera town.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, so she is a family relative.

clue.text: Rope in idle artist

blocks.note: first meaning: a nautical term for a light rope securing a boat
second meaning, read literally: a slack decorator or painter

explanation.surface: An instruction to rope in an artist who is doing no work.
explanation.walkthrough: A painter is the rope at a boat's bow; a lazy painter is the lighter one used in calm weather. 'Rope in' looks like a phrasal verb but splits into definition and link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailing term names a small mooring line, while the literal reading describes an indolent artist.

clue.text: Drink-inspired courage seen in awfully poor vault

indicators.note: awfully means very badly, so the following words are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk's bravado on show during a dreadful pole vault.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot valour is Dutch courage, bravery that comes from alcohol.

clue.text: Window a knight used during escape

indicators.note: something used during an event happens inside it, so these pieces go within

blocks.note: flight is fleeing, an escape
taken as written
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight climbs out through a window to make his getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a small, often semicircular window above a door.

clue.text: Films we saw, initially, on aquatic birds

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of saw
terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: Movies we watched about water birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Westerns are films set in the American Old West, a cinema genre.

clue.text: Film daughter playing at end of avenue

indicators.note: playing around with letters lets them move into a fresh order
the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of avenue

explanation.surface: A girl playing at the far end of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daughter' is not abbreviated to D here but used whole as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Graduate is the 1967 film starring Dustin Hoffman, an example of the category film.

clue.text: Queen entering some exceptional place of worship

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the first piece sits inside the other
exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: The Queen visits a remarkable holy building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' looks like an ordinary quantity word but is the jumbled fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosque is a Muslim building for prayer, a place of worship.

clue.text: Jack's accompanied by a pleasant girl

blocks.note: J is jack in a card pack
taken as written
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Jack is out with a lovely girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Janice is a female first name, so it fits the general word girl.

clue.text: Grotesque oaks encircling a Japanese port

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted, so the word that follows is twisted into a new order
encircling means surrounding, so the next piece sits within the first

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gnarled oak trees standing around a harbour in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city in Japan, on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: High flier up for trial?

blocks.note: surface reading: an ambitious high achiever facing a court case
setter's reading: someone literally flying high, airborne to try out a new aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'High flier' suggests a successful businessperson and 'up for trial' suggests the dock; read literally, it is a person in the air testing a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies new or modified aircraft to check how they perform, an aviator on trials.

clue.text: Previous deputy head in monastery

blocks.note: first meaning: earlier, coming before
second meaning: the monk ranking just below an abbot

explanation.walkthrough: Reads as a former deputy, but splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier in time, and a prior is the second-in-command of an abbey or head of a priory.

clue.text: Leave about ten and ring one about being impractically idealistic

indicators.note: about here means around, so the first word wraps what follows

blocks.note: to quit is to leave
X is ten in Roman numerals
O is ring-shaped
I is one in Roman numerals
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: Quitting about ten and phoning someone about a hopelessly dreamy scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' appears twice: first as the wrap-around signal, then as C, the abbreviation for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Like Don Quixote, a quixotic person chases noble but unrealistic ideals.

clue.text: Touch fringe, badly cut

indicators.note: a badly cut thing has been hacked about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feeling a fringe that a hairdresser has botched.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger something is to touch or handle it with the fingers.

clue.text: Curse banger dumped beside river

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
a crate is an old car fit for the scrapheap, a banger

explanation.surface: Swearing at an old car someone has abandoned by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger here is a battered old car, not a sausage; the river comes first in the answer though last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down curses on, a formal verb synonym.

clue.text: Very dry American statesman who committed suicide

blocks.note: brut describes very dry champagne
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A dour American politician who took his own life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American statesman' wants to be read together, but American supplies letters and the statesman is Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Brutus, Roman senator and assassin of Caesar, killed himself after defeat at Philippi.
